title: A Fairer Pathway to Settlement: Government response to the consultation (CP 1707)
key_claim: Care workers who entered or switched into the route before the May 2025 White Paper keep a five-year settlement period if they meet the £25,000 salary, sponsorship and employment requirements; those who do not can apply for a further five-year Health and Care visa restricted to genuine work in the sector; later entrants follow the 10-year path. The cohort is 196,000 care workers and 186,000 dependants, indicatively about 146,000 care workers meeting all requirements and about 50,000 needing further sponsorship; over 500,000 people will settle later than under current arrangements.
frame_summary: The government presents the care-worker carve-out as a fair, one-off transition that honours people already recruited while moving everyone else onto a longer, earned path to settlement.

title: Immigration system statistics, year ending June 2026: Why do people come to the UK? Work
key_claim: Health and Care Worker main-applicant visas peaked at 145,823 in the year ending December 2023; visas for caring occupations fell by over 99%, from 107,772 to 344, after overseas recruitment of care workers ended in July 2025; extension grants rose 19% to 336,215 in the year ending June 2026, reflecting high entry clearance grants in 2022 and 2023.
frame_summary: The statistics frame the Health and Care route as a closed inflow whose 2022 to 2023 cohort is now moving through extensions inside the UK.

key_claim: The number of internationally recruited workers in social care dropped by 40% from 2024 to 2025, partly because the care worker visa route closed, while British recruitment also fell; longer settlement waits could exacerbate recruitment challenges.
frame_summary: The Health Foundation argues that social care needs a funded workforce plan because neither domestic nor international supply is now filling posts.
